findings.name: Veterans Property Tax Exemption
findings.description: Rhode Island sets statutory minimum property tax exemption amounts for veterans (including disabled veterans), widow(er)s of veterans, and Gold Star parents under RI General Law 44-3-4, but each city and town sets its actual exemption amount by local ordinance and may vote to increase it substantially above the state minimum — the exact dollar amount therefore varies by municipality. Eligible veterans must have a discharge status other than dishonorable and served during a recognized wartime period (WWII, Korea, Vietnam, or a recognized conflict after Vietnam).
findings.value: Property tax exemption on assessed value; exact dollar amount varies by city/town ordinance
otherReqs: Service during a recognized wartime period (WWII, Korea, Vietnam, or a recognized post-Vietnam conflict)
Exemption amount and eligibility details vary by municipality
findings.agency: Rhode Island Office of Veterans Services / Town/City Tax Assessor
findings.legalCitation: RI General Law 44-3-4; RI General Law 44-3-4.2; RI General Law 44-3-5
findings.sourceExcerpt: Exemptions vary by town. Eligibility: veterans with discharge status other than dishonorable, widow(er)s of veterans, Gold Star parents, service during wartime periods (WWII, Korea, Vietnam, plus recognized conflicts after Vietnam). Apply at your town tax assessor using a DD-214.

findings.name: Disabled Veterans Tuition Waiver
findings.description: Rhode Island permanent residents who are veterans with a 10-100% VA service-connected disability rating receive free tuition at Rhode Island's public colleges and universities (Community College of Rhode Island, Rhode Island College, and University of Rhode Island). The waiver covers tuition only — fees associated with tuition continue to be charged. Applicants must first apply for and use financial aid; any scholarship aid awarded is applied to tuition in lieu of the waiver and reduces the waiver by the award amount. Recently-dated evidence of veteran status with a minimum 10% disability rating must be submitted to the Bursar's Office.
findings.value: Free tuition (fees not included) at CCRI, Rhode Island College, and URI
otherReqs: Must apply for and use financial aid first; scholarship aid reduces the waiver
Recently-dated evidence of veteran status with 10%+ disability required
findings.agency: Rhode Island Office of Veterans Services / Bursar's Office at enrolling institution
documentation: Recently-dated evidence of veteran status with a minimum 10% service-connected disability rating
findings.sourceExcerpt: Veteran with 10-100% service-connected disability qualifies for the program, which provides free tuition at RI's public colleges and universities: CCRI, Rhode Island College, and URI. The waiver applies to tuition only; fees continue to be charged.

findings.name: State of RI Veterans' Hiring Preference
findings.description: Rhode Island grants a 5-point credit on competitive civil service entrance exams to eligible veterans, and a 10-point credit to eligible disabled veterans; a passing score must be achieved before the preference is applied. A veteran must have an other-than-dishonorable discharge and 30+ days of active duty service (other than training), or have been discharged because of a service-connected disability, or be a National Guard/Reserve retiree with 20+ years of service. A disabled veteran must additionally be a war veteran (hold a campaign ribbon or expeditionary medal) with an Honorable or General discharge and a VA service-connected disability rating.
findings.value: 5-point credit on competitive civil service entrance exams for veterans; 10-point credit for disabled veterans
otherReqs: Other-than-dishonorable discharge and 30+ days active duty (non-training), OR discharge for service-connected disability, OR National Guard/Reserve retiree with 20+ years
Disabled veteran tier requires war veteran status (campaign ribbon/expeditionary medal) with Honorable or General discharge and VA service-connected rating
Must achieve a passing score before preference is applied
findings.agency: Rhode Island Office of Veterans Services / RI Division of Human Resources
documentation: DD-214 or proof of qualifying discharge and service
VA disability rating documentation for the 10-point disabled-veteran tier
findings.sourceExcerpt: RI General Law 36-4-19 establishes a hiring preference for veterans applying for competitive state positions, with veterans receiving a 5 point credit on competitive civil service entrance exams and disabled veterans receiving 10 points. Veterans must achieve a passing score before the preference is applied.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran Motor Vehicle Registration Fee Exemption
findings.description: Rhode Island veterans who, during wartime service, lost or lost the use of one or both arms, hands, feet, or legs; or received a VA grant for a specially adapted vehicle; or have a VA combined service-connected disability rating of 100%; or have been rated individually unemployable due to a service-connected disability, are completely exempt from the fee for annual registration and license to operate that motor vehicle. Certification of eligibility from the VA or other satisfactory documentation is required. The exemption applies to automobiles or commercial vehicles weighing 12,000 lbs or less.
findings.value: Complete exemption from the annual motor vehicle registration and operating license fee
otherReqs: Vehicle must be an automobile or commercial vehicle weighing 12,000 lbs or less
Certification of eligibility from the VA or other satisfactory documentation required
findings.agency: Rhode Island Division of Motor Vehicles
documentation: Discharge papers (DD-214) or equivalent military documentation
VA certification of 100% combined service-connected disability, individual unemployability, specially adapted vehicle grant, or qualifying loss of limb
findings.sourceExcerpt: Disabled veterans meeting the statutory criteria are exempt from the payment of any fee for the annual registration of and a license to operate that motor vehicle. Qualifying criteria include service-connected amputation, permanent loss of use of a limb, a combined service-connected disability rating of 100%, or individual unemployability. The exemption applies to automobiles or commercial vehicles weighing 12,000 pounds or less.

findings.name: Free Hunting and Fishing License for 100% Disabled Veterans
findings.description: Rhode Island veterans with 100% disability status from the Department of Veterans Affairs receive a permanent, no-cost license for freshwater fishing, hunting, or a freshwater fishing/hunting combo — the permanent license does not require annual renewal. These veterans are also exempt from needing a license for saltwater fishing, though they must have documentation of the qualifying VA decision available while fishing. Applicants must bring photo ID and an original document of the final VA disability decision to the RI Department of Environmental Management to apply in person, or submit those items by mail.
findings.value: Free permanent hunting/fishing license (no renewal required); saltwater fishing license not required
otherReqs: Original document of the VA's final disability decision required at application and while fishing (saltwater)
findings.agency: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management (DEM)
documentation: Original document of the VA's final disability decision(s) on agency letterhead
findings.sourceExcerpt: Veterans qualifying for no-cost licenses must have 100% disability status from the Department of Veterans Affairs. Disabled veterans meeting this threshold receive permanent licenses for freshwater fishing, hunting, and freshwater fishing/hunting combo, and are exempt from needing a license for saltwater fishing.
